\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Nondeterministic termination relation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NTerm}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NTerm}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.nastep}
For a nondeterministic register program $A$, an oracle, an input $x$, and a guard $G$ on
configurations, define termination under the guard inductively as follows. Every halted
configuration terminates; a live configuration terminates when it satisfies $G$ and both
configurations reached by the two possible choice bits terminate.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Acceptance by a choice sequence]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NAcc}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NAcc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.narun}
A configuration is accepting for a nondeterministic register program $A$, oracle, and
input $x$ if there is a finite bit string of choices such that running $A$ from that
configuration with those choices halts and returns true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Nondeterministic program semantics]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NSem}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NSem}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NARM, Complexity.LogProg.NAcc, Complexity.LogProg.NTerm}
For a nondeterministic register program $A$, an oracle, an input $x$, a guard $G$ on
configurations, an initial configuration $a$, and a proposition $P$, define the
semantics to mean that $A$ terminates from $a$ under guard $G$ and that $a$ is accepting
if and only if $P$ holds.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Register bound on a configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.RegLe}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.RegLe}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf}
Let $m$ and $B$ be natural numbers, let $\Lambda$ be a type, and let $a$ be a
configuration with $m$ registers and labels in $\Lambda$. Say that $a$ satisfies the
register bound $B$ if every register contains a natural number at most $B$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform halting bound]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NTerm.nhalts}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NTerm.nhalts}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.halted, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts.mono_len, Complexity.LogProg.NTerm, Complexity.LogProg.narun_cons, Complexity.LogProg.nastep}
\difficulty{5}
Let a nondeterministic register program with oracle, input, and guard be fixed, and let
$a$ be a configuration from which every branch terminates while satisfying the guard at
each live intermediate configuration. Then there is a natural number $N$ such that every
choice string of length $N$ leads from $a$ to a halted configuration, and for every
shorter prefix of such a string, if the resulting configuration is still live then it
satisfies the guard.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Acceptance from a Halted Configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.nacc_halted}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.nacc_halted}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NAcc}
\difficulty{3}
For any nondeterministic register program, oracle, input, register assignment $v$, and
optional recorded Boolean answer $res$, the halted configuration with registers $v$ and
answer $res$ is accepting if and only if $res$ is true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Acceptance from a Live Configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.nacc_live}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.nacc_live}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NAcc, Complexity.LogProg.nastep}
\difficulty{4}
For a nondeterministic register machine $A$, oracle, input $x$, control state $l$, and
register valuation $v$, a configuration with state $l$, valuation $v$, and no recorded
answer has an accepting run if and only if there is a choice bit $b$ such that the
configuration after one step using $b$ has an accepting run.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Deterministic Instruction Step]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.nastep_det'}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.nastep_det'}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.astep, Complexity.LogProg.nastep}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program, let an oracle assign a Boolean answer to
each decider and bit string, and fix an input word, a program state $l$, and a
deterministic instruction $i$. If $A$ assigns the deterministic instruction $i$ to $l$,
then for any choice bit $b$, register valuation, and optional result, one step of the
nondeterministic program from state $l$ agrees with one step of the deterministic
program that assigns instruction $i$ to every state.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Invariance Under Equivalent Propositions]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NSem.congr}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NSem.congr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NSem}
\difficulty{1}
For a fixed nondeterministic register machine, oracle, input, guard, and configuration,
if the configuration satisfies the termination and acceptance semantics for proposition
$P$, and $P$ is logically equivalent to $Q$, then it satisfies those semantics for $Q$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Semantics of a Halted Configuration]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NSem.halted}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NSem.halted}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NSem, Complexity.LogProg.nacc_halted}
\difficulty{3}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with oracle, input $x$, and configuration
guard $G$. For any register valuation $v$ and Boolean answer $b$, the configuration with
no live state, valuation $v$, and stored answer $b$ is terminating under $G$ and accepts
exactly when $b$ is true.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Preservation Across a Deterministic Instruction]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NSem.det}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NSem.det}

\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with oracle, input $x$, and configuration
guard $G$. Suppose the instruction at live state $l$ is the deterministic instruction
$i$, and the configuration with state $l$, register valuation $v$, and no answer
satisfies $G$. If the configuration obtained by executing $i$ from there is terminating
under $G$ and accepts exactly when proposition $P$ holds, then the original
configuration has those same properties.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Semantics of a Nondeterministic Choice]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NSem.choose}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NSem.choose}

\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine, with oracle, input bit string, and
configuration guard $G$ fixed. If the instruction at control state $l$ chooses between
$l_1$ and $l_0$, the configuration at $l$ satisfies $G$, and the successor
configurations at $l_1$ and $l_0$ satisfy the termination and acceptance semantics for
propositions $P_1$ and $P_0$, respectively, then the configuration at $l$ satisfies
those semantics for $P_1 \lor P_0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Semantics of a decrement instruction]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.nsem_dec}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.nsem_dec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NSem, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.det, Complexity.LogProg.astep}
\difficulty{1}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program, $O$ an oracle family, $x$ an input bit
string, and $G$ a guard on configurations. Suppose the instruction at state $l$
decrements register $r$ (with subtraction truncated at zero) and proceeds to state $l'$.
If $G$ holds at $(l,v,\mathrm{none})$, then for any proposition $P$, terminating
semantics and acceptance equivalent to $P$ at $(l',v',\mathrm{none})$, where
$v'(r)=\max(v(r)-1,0)$ and all other register values agree with $v$, imply the same
semantics at $(l,v,\mathrm{none})$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Finite-Time Characterisation of Acceptance]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.NSem.decides}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.NSem.decides}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AConf, Complexity.LogProg.NAns, Complexity.LogProg.NHalts, Complexity.LogProg.NSem, Complexity.LogProg.NTerm.nhalts, Complexity.LogProg.narun_append_of_halted}
\difficulty{5}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register machine with oracle, input $x$, configuration
guard $G$, initial configuration $a$, and proposition $P$. Suppose every computation
from $a$ terminates and every live configuration reached before termination satisfies
$G$, and suppose $P$ holds exactly when some finite computation from $a$ halts with
answer true. Then there is a number $N$ such that every sequence of $N$ choice bits
leads to a halted configuration, every live configuration along each such computation
before step $N$ satisfies $G$, and $P$ holds exactly when some sequence of $N$ choice
bits leads to answer true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nondeterministic interval guess]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.nsem_guess}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.nsem_guess}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NSem, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.choose, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.congr, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.ret, Complexity.LogProg.RegLe, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with oracle, let $x$ be an input, and let
$B$ be a register bound. Choose distinct registers $g,nr$ and states
$test,ch,more,ex,rej$. Suppose the deterministic instruction at $test$ compares $g$ with
$nr$, branching to $rej$ when they are equal and to $ch$ otherwise; at $ch$ the program
may choose $ex$ or $more$; at $more$ it increments $g$ and returns to $test$; and at
$rej$ it halts with answer false. Let $Q$ be a predicate on natural numbers, and let $v$
be an initial register assignment with every register at most $B$ and $v(g)\le v(nr)$.
If, for every $j$ with $v(g)\le j<v(nr)$, the configuration at $ex$ with $g$ set to $j$
and all other registers unchanged terminates within the register bound and accepts
exactly when $Q(j)$ holds, then the configuration at $test$ with assignment $v$
terminates within that bound and accepts exactly when some $j$ in that interval
satisfies $Q(j)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Semantics of copying a register]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.nsem_copy}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.nsem_copy}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NSem, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.RegLe, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers, oracle family $O$,
input $x$, and space bound $B$. Let $\mathrm{dst}$ and $\mathrm{src}$ be distinct
registers, and suppose the instruction at $\mathrm{test}$ compares them, branching to
$\mathrm{ex}$ on equality and to $\mathrm{bump}$ otherwise, while the instruction at
$\mathrm{bump}$ increments $\mathrm{dst}$ and returns to $\mathrm{test}$. If every
current register value is at most $B$ and $v(\mathrm{dst})\le v(\mathrm{src})$, then for
any proposition $P$, terminating semantics under the register bound $B$ and acceptance
equivalent to $P$ at the configuration with $\mathrm{dst}$ replaced by $v(\mathrm{src})$
imply the same semantics at the original configuration
$(\mathrm{test},v,\mathrm{none})$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Semantics of a two-step register addition]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.nsem_addTwice}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.nsem_addTwice}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.NSem, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.inc, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_neg, Complexity.LogProg.NSem.jeq_pos, Complexity.LogProg.RegLe, Complexity.LogProg.register_update_le}
\difficulty{6}
Let $A$ be a nondeterministic register program with $m$ registers, oracle family $O$,
input $x$, and space bound $B$. Let $k,y,p$ be registers with $k\ne y$, $k\ne p$, and
$p\ne y$, and suppose the instruction at state $\mathrm{test}$ compares registers $k$
and $y$, branching to $\mathrm{ex}$ on equality and to $i_1$ otherwise; the instructions
at $i_1$ and $i_2$ each increment $p$ and proceed respectively to $i_2$ and $i_3$, and
the instruction at $i_3$ increments $k$ and returns to $\mathrm{test}$. If the current
register values $v(r)$ are all at most $B$, $v(k)\le v(y)$, and $v(p)+2(v(y)-v(k))\le
B$, then for any proposition $P$, if the configuration at $\mathrm{ex}$ with $p$
replaced by $v(p)+2(v(y)-v(k))$ and $k$ replaced by $v(y)$ has terminating
nondeterministic semantics with space guard $B$ and acceptance equivalent to $P$, the
configuration at $\mathrm{test}$ with the original register values has the same
semantics.
\end{theorem}
